subject.title: [Refactor] Gateway Session Shutdown Tracker: Bounded Memory Footprint, Configurable Timeout, and Safe Abort Signal Handling

question: Should the shipped fixed shutdown budget and session_end plugin contract become publicly configurable and cancellable, or should this remain an internal lifecycle policy?
rationale: The bounded timeout, captured configuration context, and active-run cleanup ordering were intentional reviewed choices; changing them requires product and plugin-contract ownership rather than a mechanical refactor.

options.title: Internal bounded follow-up
options.body: Reduce retained context and supervise overdue work without adding configuration or changing the session_end API.

options.title: Add public cancellation controls
options.body: Introduce a documented timeout and additive AbortSignal contract with fresh-install, upgrade, shutdown-grace, and plugin compatibility proof.

options.title: Retain shipped design
options.body: Leave the implementation unchanged unless realistic measurements demonstrate material memory or resource growth.

recommendation.title: Internal bounded follow-up
recommendation.body: Reduce retained context and supervise overdue work without adding configuration or changing the session_end API.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the original feature and directly established the concurrent fixed-budget semantics under review.
